title: transaction_record
description: A record that money moved: from whom, to whom, how much, how and when. It is a record for provenance and does not replace or perform the transaction itself; the real transaction lives in the payment system, the bank or the cash drawer. Other records (such as a registration_assignment) hold only this record's id, never payment details. Never store card numbers, bank account numbers or other payment credentials, here or anywhere. A refund is a new record (transaction_type refund) that points at the payment it refunds with refund_of_id; an existing record is never edited to become a refund. Fields marked readOnly are set by the server only. Endpoint rules the schema cannot express: refund_of_id must name an existing record of type payment, and a refund's amount_cents may not exceed that payment's amount_cents less refunds already recorded.

transaction_type.description: payment (money in), refund (money back out, linked to the payment by refund_of_id) or adjustment (a correction or write-off). Required.

payer.description: Who the money came from. Required.

party_type.description: What kind of party: person, organization or program (for example the workshop program itself receiving money). Required.

name.description: The party's name as it should read on the record. Required.

party_id.description: UUID of the party's own record, when one exists (a person, organization or program record; none are written yet). Optional.

payee.description: Who the money went to. Required.

party_type.description: What kind of party: person, organization or program (for example the workshop program itself receiving money). Required.

name.description: The party's name as it should read on the record. Required.

party_id.description: UUID of the party's own record, when one exists (a person, organization or program record; none are written yet). Optional.

amount_cents.description: The amount in whole US cents. Never negative: direction is carried by transaction_type, payer and payee. Required.

method.description: How it was paid: card_processor (through a third-party processor; the processor holds the card), cash, check, bank_transfer or other. Required.

external_source.description: The outside system that holds the real transaction, for example a processor's name. Optional.

external_reference.description: The outside system's id for the transaction, such as a processor's payment id or a check number. Never card or account details. Optional.

status.description: pending (expected or processing), completed (money moved), failed (it did not go through) or voided (cancelled before completing). A refund is a separate record, not a status. Required.

occurred_at.description: When the money moved, or was expected to. Sent by the dashboard or handler because a transaction may be recorded later than it happened. Required.

refund_of_id.description: UUID of the payment this refund refunds. Required on a refund and not allowed on any other type.

note.description: Anything worth remembering about the transaction, in the organizer's words. Never card or account details.

program_slug.description: Which program the transaction belongs to, as a slug such as launch. Set by the server.

id.description: UUID v4, set by the server; also the Firestore document id. Never sent by a browser.

schema_version.description: Version of this schema the record was written under (currently 1). Set by the server.

created_at.description: When the record was created. Set by the server.

created_by.description: Who created the record, as an actor string such as user:<uuid> or system:<handler>. Set by the server.

updated_at.description: When the record was last changed. Set by the server.

updated_by.description: Who last changed the record, as an actor string. Set by the server.

source.description: Where the record came from: dashboard, import or system (an automated handler, for example a payment webhook). Set by the server.

previous_id.description: Id of the earlier record this one follows or replaces. Set by the server.

deleted_at.description: When the record was soft deleted. Records are never hard deleted. Set by the server.

deleted_by.description: Who soft deleted the record, as an actor string. Set by the server.
